newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Abdur Rahman Biswas is packing up to leave the presidential palace, Bangabhaban, on Tuesday completing his full five-year tenure. Biswas is the first Bangladeshi president who could complete full term.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has warned action against doctors who remain absent in remote rural health centres. "This is unfortunate. You must not forget that you are being paid from taxes of common people," she told the doctors.
Bangladesh is considering to import 100-200 megawatt of electricity from India to meet the short-term pressing needs of the country, said chief of Bangladesh Power Development Board.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has announced that low income groups would get soft-term loans to meet their housing demands.

Abul Khair, the nine-year-old boy who saved more than 1,000 lives by his quick-witted action that helped avert a train disaster, has been named Reader's Digest "Hero for Today" in October, the first Bangladeshi awarded with the distinction.

The Malaysian government is expected to take fresh manpower from Bangladesh from early next year, said Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Abul Hasan Chowdhury who visited Kuala Lampur last month.
